name: Obadiah
overview: Obadiah was a male Levite known specifically as the son of Shemaiah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:16. His identification within the tribe of Levi situates him among the priestly lineage entrusted with religious duties in Israel. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Obadiah means 'servant [worshiper] of YHWH,' reflecting a life dedicated to the Lord, consistent with his Levitical heritage. Another form of his name, Abda, similarly means 'servant of YHWH,' emphasizing his role as a devoted follower of God. Both names highlight a servant relationship to the Lord but were not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Obadiah is explicitly identified as the son of Shemaiah, establishing a clear familial link within the Levitical line. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Obadiah's significance in Scripture lies primarily in his Levitical heritage and his identification as the son of Shemaiah, marking him as part of the priestly families responsible for maintaining worship and service to God. His names underscore a life devoted to serving YHWH, aligning with the spiritual duties of the Levites. Although brief, his mention contributes to the genealogical and religious context of the post-exilic community.
